When SpaceX isn't busy with rockets, it turns out it's closing deals with AI companies. Back in February, the company behind Starlink swallowed up xAI, which includes Twitter, now known as X. In April this year, SpaceX signed a deal with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. As of August 14th, the acquisition is complete. The company, now renamed SpaceXAI, recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's help.

Update August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed the acquisition of Cursor.

Update June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after becoming a publicly listed company.

Below is an updated version of the original report:

SpaceX and Cursor reach US$10 billion deal, followed by another US$60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who write AI programmes on Mac. It was one of the first services to connect large language model AI into the application development workflow.

In April this year, the two companies stated that SpaceX and Cursor were "working closely together, with the goal of creating the world's top programming and knowledge work AI."

This collaboration originally included the US$10 billion SpaceX gave to Cursor:

Cursor, in April this year and before today's acquisition, shared more details about the arrangement:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. Composer was our first agentic coding model, released less than six months ago. Following that, Composer 1.5 scaled up reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. After that, Composer 2 added continual pre-training, achieving frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Each level of increased computing power translates into a substantially stronger model. We've always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by computing bottlenecks. Through this partnership, our team will use xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically improve the intelligence level of our models.

The SpaceX and Cursor partnership positions itself as a competitor to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex agentic coding software.
